Items 3 and 4 are pre-flight guards and may land before w1/w2 if helpful,
but do not attempt the lock bump (w5) until both gates are resolved. Keep
the pre-flight changes minimal. The lock bump (w5) is the verification step,
not the starting point.

For the modin gate: watch modin's GitHub releases page and pyproject.toml

3.11 in a separate, clearly-scoped commit before this item starts - that
avoids environment-marker complexity in pyproject.toml.
description:
pandas 3.0.2 is available on PyPI but cannot be safely bumped yet.
A compatibility evaluation (2026-04-22) found two hard blockers that must
clear before the actual lock bump begins, plus two targeted code fixes needed before
the lock bump lands.

── HARD BLOCKERS (do not proceed until both are resolved) ──────────────────

1. modin 0.37.1 requires `pandas<2.4,>=2.2`.
   `uv lock --upgrade-package pandas` fails to resolve because modin's upper
   bound (`<2.4`) and pandas 3.x are mutually exclusive. No modin release
   beyond 0.37.1 exists as of 2026-04-22 that relaxes this cap. Modin is a
   first-class BenchBox platform (benchbox/platforms/dataframe/modin_df.py,
   extras modin / dataframe-pandas-family / all) - silently excluding it
   from the resolved environment is not acceptable.
   Watch: https://github.com/modin-project/modin/releases

2. pandas 3.0 requires Python ≥ 3.11.
   BenchBox declares `requires-python = ">=3.10,<3.15"`. Bumping pandas
   would silently break Python 3.10 users. Either (a) raise the project
   minimum to 3.11 (requires a separate decision and full CI matrix change)
   or (b) confirm that pandas can remain at 2.x for Python 3.10 via
   environment markers - and verify uv resolves that correctly.

── PRE-FLIGHT CODE FIXES (required before lock bump, no behaviour change) ──

3. pandas_df.py:145-155 - `pd.options.mode.copy_on_write` assignment.
   In pandas 3.0 this option is deprecated and a no-op. The current code
   sets it unconditionally (guarded only by `pandas_version >= (2, 0)`).
   Fix: add an upper guard `pandas_version < (3, 0)` so the assignment is
   skipped on 3.x where CoW is always active.

4. TPC-DI ingest datetime resolution.
   pandas 3.0 defaults to microsecond resolution for datetime parsing
   (vs. nanoseconds in 2.x). Any remaining code in `tpcdi/benchmark.py` that
   reads or normalizes date/time values via pd.read_csv / pd.read_fwf /
   pd.read_json / pd.to_datetime and then converts to int64 or compares
   values numerically can produce 1000× different results under 3.x. Audit and add
   explicit `dtype_backend`, `parse_dates=False`, or explicit resolution
   normalization where the downstream code is resolution-sensitive. (CoW
   in-place mutation audit was clean - no fixes needed there.)

── EVALUATION SUMMARY ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Evaluated 2026-04-22. pandas 3.x breaking changes cross-referenced against
BenchBox codebase:
- DataFrame.swapaxes / append / Index.format() - not used, no impact.
- groupby/resample keyword changes - not used in DataFrame platform layer.
- datetime-unit changes in read/normalize paths - affects the remaining
  TPC-DI benchmark ingest path only (item 4).
- CoW mandatory - in-place mutation audit clean; only item 3 needs a guard.
Estimated effort once gates clear: 1-2 days.
